content.title: Asymmetric Breach | Dense Resistance Changes the Space
content.summary: Establish a defended target and a dense resistance field, then introduce one asymmetric moving force. Use local contacts to prove momentum and wide views to prove advance; after the breach, make the spatial regime visibly different and hold the close consequence.

quick_start.input_format: Fixed target + dense resistance field + single asymmetric force + 3 local contacts + breakthrough to change space
quick_start.recommended_input: In the flooded logistics hall, an unmanned tugboat cleared the foam obstacle channel through three visible contacts, and once again pushed the rescue gate open to allow three small boats to pass through in sequence.
required_anchors: Establish one fixed objective and a dense visible resistance field.
Introduce one asymmetric force with a clear motion axis.
Return wide to show progress toward the boundary.
Let one breach change the spatial regime and hold the consequence.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Establish a defended target and a dense resistance field, then introduce one asymmetric moving force. Use local contacts to prove momentum and wide views to prove advance; after the breach, make the spatial regime visibly different and hold the close consequence.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish a fortified objective and dense resisting field, introduce one asymmetric moving force, prove momentum through several local contacts, widen to show progress toward the objective, then use one breach to change the spatial regime before a close held consequence.

invariants.rule: Establish one fixed objective and a dense visible resistance field.
Introduce one asymmetric force with a clear motion axis.
invariants.ablation_failure: Several equal forces create generic chaos.

invariants.rule: Use multiple local contacts to prove momentum.
invariants.ablation_failure: A distant charge alone does not prove force.

invariants.rule: Return wide to show progress toward the boundary.
invariants.ablation_failure: Only close action hides whether progress occurred.

invariants.rule: Let one breach change the spatial regime and hold the consequence.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending before entry leaves the objective unresolved.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair whose role is clear without source identity.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A materially new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific location.

slots.name: causal_carrier
slots.constraint: One object, route, mark or device that visibly carries the causal chain.

slots.name: state_change
slots.constraint: Five ordered states with observable handoffs, not a decorative montage.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: A new proof-oriented information order that does not copy source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A held final consequence that resolves or recontextualizes the setup.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of story-world cues supporting each visible change.

anti_copy_exclusions: source fantasy beast and armored army
castle gate, siege field and fire
the exact creature charge and breach choreography
source medieval costume and weapon design
